thread:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert: high CPU on tokenizer-preproc pods in prod-us-west-2 (svc: tokenizer, severity: P1) :rotating_light:
incident-bot: Affected: 12/24 pods Restarting due to OOMKill. Error: 'Out of memory: Killed process 12345 (python) total-vm:...'
incident-bot: Initial metric spike started at 2026-03-15T10:13:18Z (thread root).
emma: ack — I'm on it. grabbing logs now.
sanjay: oncall-sre taking pager. can you paste last 5 lines of kubelet + container logs?
lex: seeing rapid tokenization latency increase in the trace stream for requests hitting tokenizer-v2.
olivia: customer-impact: a handful of high-QPS enterprise tenants experienced 503s and increased latency. CS is alerted. @customer-success please assemble the list.
oncall-sre: taking lead on infra. initial observation: CPU is pegged at 100% for the preproc container, OOM triggers kernel OOM killer. Pods are stuck in CrashLoopBackOff.
ml-runtime: looks like a prompt with extremely long repeated delimiters triggered backtracking in our regex tokenizer. we've seen similar once in staging.
emma: found one sample in logs: ``"prompt":"<user>...<repeated '>' char ~120k>..."``. bad client input.
sanjay: good catch. mitigation plan: 1) scale tokenizer replicas down to 2 and set concurrency to 1 to reduce pressure, 2) apply CPU limit to preproc container so OOM is node-contained, 3) deploy hotfix to reject >10k char tokens at gateway.
lex: can we route traffic to tokenizer-v1 variant while we patch v2? v1 has lower perf but stable.
oncall-sre: doing quick canary switch: patching service selector to prefer tokenizer-v1 for 10% traffic, then 100% if stable.
deploy-bot: deploy started by oncall-sre: patch/service/tokenizer-traffic-shift @ 1885012145
emma: running one-off script to drop long-prompt requests at the ingress, snippet below:
```
# nginx lua filter pseudo
local maxchars = 10000
if #req.body > maxchars then
  ngx.status = 413
  ngx.say('Payload too large')
  return ngx.exit(413)
end
```
ml-runtime: pushing tokenizer regex guard to runtime repo now. will include a fallback that returns a nice error instead of blowing the tokenizer.
lex: also throttling internal batcher: set BATCH_MAX = 8 temporarily.
oncall-sre: executed `kubectl scale deployment/tokenizer-v2 --replicas=2 -n prod` and `kubectl patch deployment tokenizer-v2 -p '{"spec":{"template":{"spec":{"containers":[{"name":"preproc","resources":{"limits":{"cpu":"500m","memory":"512Mi"}}}]}}}}'` — applied @1885012280
sanjay: cordoning overloaded node ip-10-2-7-45 and draining pods off it: `kubectl cordon ip-10-2-7-45 && kubectl drain ip-10-2-7-45 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data` @1885012350
olivia: CS: sending note to impacted customers: short message + ETA for mitigation. "We observed intermittent 503s affecting tokenization-heavy requests; mitigation in progress, partial rollback to stable variant; we'll follow up."
customer-success: posting banner now and sending targeted emails to three enterprise tenants we identified.
emma: after traffic shift / rate-limit, CPU stress is dropping on v2 replicas from 98% -> 45% over last 60s. Pod restarts reduced.
oncall-sre: observed 0 OOM events in past 5m on patched replicas. node memory reclaim stabilizing.
ml-runtime: hotfix PR created: add guard to tokenizer to short-circuit extremely long runs and log the offending prompt id. PR: https://git.internal/redwood/ml-runtime/pulls/4567 @1885012550
lex: can we add a lightweight pre-filter in the api-gateway to detect repetitive-delimiter attacks? I'd rather not rely solely on model-side checks.
sanjay: agreed. I'll raise a task to add heuristic filters to gateway and rate-limiters.
deploy-bot: deploy succeeded: tokenizer-traffic-shift -> 10% v1 @1885012600
emma: oncall handoff in ~20m to @lex. current status: mitigations in place, CPU normalized, patch PR open, CS notified, monitoring dashboards green for the last 3m.
lex: taking the handoff. will watch for regressions and coordinate with ml-runtime to merge hotfix after tests.
oncall-sre: recommendations for postmortem: - root cause: unbounded prompt length with pathological delimiter pattern triggering tokenizer backtracking -> CPU blowup -> OOM. - gaps: no pre-filter at gateway, tokenization not defensive. - mitigations: immediate traffic shift, CPU limits, ingress guard, tokenizer quick-fail + logging, gateway heuristics, add e2e test with long-delimiter fuzz.
ml-runtime: adding a feature flag to enable defensive tokenization with cheap O(n) checks. will measure perf impact in canary.
customer-success: emailed tenants with incident summary + workaround: sanitize inputs and enforce client-side limits.
emma: leaving notes in incident channel and runbook updated with commands used and thresholds.
incident-bot: Incident P1 acknowledged by oncall-sre. Status: Mitigated -> Monitoring.
lex: final note before handoff: keep an eye on nodes that drained; sometimes evicted pods requeue and cause transient spikes. if we see CPU creep, re-open pager. :eyes:
customer-success: customers replied appreciative of fast mitigation. one asked for a postmortem and SLA credit request.
ml-runtime: tagging PR for expedited review. will follow up in #eng-ml postmortem thread.
lex: handing off to next oncall (mira) in 15. I'll post a short summary to the incidents channel once postmortem draft is ready.
incident-bot: Thread closed by lex at 2026-03-15T10:41:20Z (status: monitoring).
